annotations.title: Check if a Service Is Down

description: Do RealUptime's own checks of a third-party service currently fail, from named regions? A check is one unauthenticated request to the service's front door; it says whether that check passed or failed, not whether the service works for users. Returns a verdict of "up" (our checks pass), "down" (our checks fail), "down_in_some_regions" (our checks fail from some regions), "blocked", "no_data", or "not_covered" (the service is not in RealUptime's catalog). When the service's status feed works, `vendor` carries what the vendor itself declares on its status page, and the verdict, `verdict_source` and plate then come from that declaration alone (down while its live incident is rated major or critical, otherwise up); our own reading is `checks_reading`, shown beside it. Also returns `plate`, the public page's headline: one level from down / partially_down / degraded / partially_degraded / reachable_reports_elevated / blocked / no_data / partially_unverified / up, with its label and the sentence under it. "reachable_reports_elevated" means our checks pass but user reports or public chatter are above their spike threshold: NOT a failed check, and never to be quoted as one. Pass `region` (iad = US-East, sjc = US-West, fra = Europe, nrt = Asia-Pacific) to ask about one region only. Readings are RealUptime's own check readings, never user reports. For a service whose status feed we can read, `vendor.feed_working` is true and `vendor` holds the vendor's own declared incident from its status page: that statement leads and gives the verdict and plate, and `checks_reading` and `vendor.regional_reading` are our check reading beside it, never a second outage. Where we cannot read a feed (`vendor.feed_working` false), the answer is our checks alone. "blocked" means our check was refused, which is NOT a failed check of the service. A no-data answer is never a passing check. Our check readings are our own reading from outside, not the service's official status. `check_evidence`, when it is not null, says what a pass of this service's check shows and does not show: repeat it with any claim that the service works. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: is_service_down
